title: Two-axis operation-correlated effective-behavior evidence
purpose: Satisfy REQ-QUIC-CRT-0206 through REQ-QUIC-CRT-0209 by closing the correctness-only evidence chain for application_send_batch_formation and buffer_copy_coalescing without releasing measurement, interaction execution, active_internal, or production behavior.
design_summary: Each seam emits immutable fixed-field evidence for configured, forced, shadow-recommended, pre-safety candidate, operation eligibility, applied value, mechanism event, legal and applied work, and bounded correlation. Batch decisions latch to one packet plan; buffer decisions latch through the combined owner lifetime and exactly one terminal release. A deterministic PowerShell materializer resolves the reviewed behavior catalog and maps only axis-specific mechanism events to effective behavior IDs. It emits bounded per-epoch aggregates and a rebuildable logical projection whose authority remains the immutable checksummed artifact chain.
data_and_state_considerations: Connection-local numeric epoch, decision-instance, operation, upstream-plan, and release identities avoid per-operation strings and allocations in the runtime. Operation rows may be retained only by an explicitly bounded diagnostic sink; fixed counters are the normal epoch evidence. Offline documents use canonical UTF-8 JSON and SHA-256 with the root content_sha256 excluded. Invalid, inactive, clamped, fallback, negative, excluded, and diagnostic rows remain append-only inputs to materialization and projection.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A shadow recommendation is a candidate fact and never changes the applied mechanism.
A forced candidate may be clamped or rejected and never bypasses operation eligibility or an authoritative transport guard.
A broad buffer-copy or endpoint event is not buffer_copy_coalescing mechanism evidence.
One epoch may contain several effective behavior IDs when different operations prove different mechanisms.
One operation cannot receive mutually exclusive behavior IDs.
Unclassifiable evidence is retained as invalid and is never assigned a guessed behavior.
The send-composition interaction remains capability-pending and the current one-behavior-distinct-axis runtime guard remains unchanged.
alternatives_considered: Infer behavior from applied value alone. Rejected because inactive and clamped operations can execute a different mechanism than the candidate label suggests.
Infer behavior from throughput, latency, CPU, or allocation totals. Rejected because those are performance outcomes, not mechanism evidence.
Persist every operation without bounds. Rejected because runtime retention must remain bounded and allocation-conscious.
Select a database as the evidence authority. Rejected because the projection must rebuild from immutable checksummed artifacts.
risks: Publishing at a planning boundary can overstate a committed mechanism unless no-plan and unclassifiable states remain explicit.
Buffer release can occur in a later epoch, so decision epoch and release epoch must remain distinct.
Catalog drift can silently relabel behavior unless identity, version, and hash are checked together.
A cross-axis fixture can be mistaken for newly executable interaction capability unless the capability-pending boundary remains explicit.
open_questions: Which bounded sampled-operation retention rate, if any, should be approved for later live campaigns?
Which capability proof would separately release send-composition interaction execution?
Which remaining implemented axis should receive the next reviewed evidence migration?
